newsitem.title: DUBAI: Israeli companies not welcome in Dubai - official.
newsitem.headline: Israeli companies not welcome in Dubai - official.

text.p: Israeli companies are still not welcome to set up operations in the United Arab Emirates' (UAE) trading centre of Dubai, an official said in remarks published on Wednesday.

"There will be no presence for Israeli companies in Dubai or in Jebel Ali Free Zone," Mohammad Alabbar, director general of Dubai's Economic Department, was quoted by the Arabic-language al-Khaleej newspaper as saying.
"We have a liberal economy and an open market, but when it comes to Israel we are at the end of the march," he said.

The Gulf Cooperation Council -- grouping Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Bahrain, Oman, Qatar and Kuwait -- supports the Middle East peace process but will only set up diplomatic ties with the Jewish state once there is a full Arab-Israeli settlement.
But Qatar and Oman have forged ahead of their GCC partners in establishing economic links with Israel, allowing it to set up trade missions in Doha and Muscat.
Dubai has attracted scores of international firms particularly in its Jebel Ali Free Zone, which hosts 930 companies from 72 countries with investments of about $1.6 billion dollars.
